case_notes: Tests whether the pipeline still flags victim status as negative when it is described indirectly with euphemistic language (an 'incident', someone 'shaken but unharmed', a break-in without the word crime), rather than explicit crime/legal terms, and when a distractor positive source is present that has nothing to do with the victimization.
expected_failure_modes: may miss indirect or euphemistic victim language such as 'incident' or 'break-in' that never uses explicit crime words
may weight the unrelated positive volunteer source too heavily and produce an overall positive or neutral result
may treat 'recovering' and 'support' language as purely positive rather than as a signal of harm requiring review

sources.title: Daniel Kim Reflects on a Difficult Spring and the Path Back to Normal
sources.article_text:
Daniel Kim says the last few months have not been easy. Since an unsettling incident at his home back in March, he has been taking things one day at a time, leaning on a few close friends and a counselor he started seeing shortly afterward.

'I used to not think twice about falling asleep with a window cracked open. That's just different for me now,' Kim said, describing how his sense of safety at home was upended almost overnight. He declined to go into detail about exactly what happened that night, saying only that it involved someone who was not supposed to be there.

Kim said he has appreciated the patience of his coworkers as he adjusted his schedule to make time for appointments related to his recovery. He said he is slowly starting to feel more like himself, though certain sounds at night still catch him off guard.

Friends describe Kim as private but resilient, and say they have tried to check in regularly without pushing him to talk before he is ready.

sources.title: Maple Street Neighbors Rally After Break-In Leaves Resident Shaken
sources.article_text:
Residents of the Maple Street neighborhood are checking in on each other more often after a break-in at Daniel Kim's home last month left the longtime resident shaken but unharmed. Neighbors said Kim was home at the time and briefly confronted the intruder before the person fled through a back door.

Neighbor Sarah Chen said the block has since started a group chat to share updates and keep an eye on each other's homes in the evenings. 'We just want Daniel to know people are paying attention and he's not dealing with this alone,' Chen said.

Kim has installed new locks and a doorbell camera since the incident. He declined to comment further, but a close friend said he has seemed more on edge than usual and has been taking some time before returning to his normal routine.

sources.title: Daniel Kim Marks Third Year Volunteering at Westside Public Library
sources.article_text:
Daniel Kim was recognized this week for completing three years as a weekly volunteer at the Westside Public Library, where he helps run the children's reading hour every Wednesday afternoon. Library staff said Kim rarely misses a session and has become a familiar, welcome face to families who attend regularly.

Branch manager Louis Ferreira said Kim has a gift for keeping young children engaged during story time and often brings in props or simple crafts tied to that week's book. 'Parents specifically ask if Daniel is reading before they decide which day to come in,' Ferreira said.

Kim said he started volunteering as a way to give back after moving to the neighborhood and has enjoyed watching some of the same kids grow up over the past three years. The library plans to recognize Kim's contribution with a small certificate at its spring volunteer appreciation event.
